thread:
IncBot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: GPU_PREEMPT_SURGE in us-west2 affecting gpu-serving pools. Alert: queue depth rising > 1200, avg token latency spiking. Trigger: spot eviction + autoscaler errors.

maya: @here seeing a lot of preempts from the cloud side, spot pool drained ~40% in last 3m. Queues for long-seq endpoints (chat & completion) now > 1k.

liam: Oncall, jumping in. Any immediate mitigation in runbook?

maya: Runbook suggests fallback to reserved/dedicated pools + temporary rate-limit. I can flip throttles while we validate fallback routes.

sara: autoscaler logs show repeated 429s from cloud quota API, then HPA failing to scale due to `scaleUpForbidden` from our controller. Looks like rate-limited instance provisioning, not our kube. Pasting recent log: ```2026-03-15T03:12:05Z controller: provisioner request failed status=429 body="QuotaExceeded"```.

liam: That explains why spot preemptions aren't being backfilled. Can we route new requests to dedicated pool `dedicated-usw2-v2`? Is there enough headroom?

aditi_cs: CS reports 4 customers seeing 500s and higher latency. One enterprise tenant on dedicated plan still ok but shared-hosted customers impacted. Tickets coming in.

maya: Quick plan: 1) Throttle long-seq endpoints to 30 rps 2) Route new short-seq traffic to cheaper on-demand model variants 3) Enable fallback traffic to `dedicated-usw2-v2` (need infra approval) 4) If insufficient, enable emergency burst (billing + contract).

liam: I'll try patching routing policies. Running command now: ```rtrctl update-policy --from=hosted-usw2 --to=dedicated-usw2-v2 --match=seq<=512 --percentage=60```.

ops-monitor: autoscaler controller: retrying provisioning, 3/5 attempts failed. Errors: [QuotaExceeded, RateLimitExceeded, InternalError].

sara: FYI, spot provider is returning preempt list with high churn. We should avoid re-scheduling spot-only workloads to the same pool. I'll add a temporary affinity label to prevent bounce. ```kubectl label ns batch-spot avoid-redeploy=preemptive-temp```

maya: Throttle applied to chat/completion (long-seq) to 30 rps. Route update in flight.

liam: Policy applied, 55% routed to dedicated for seq<=512, 5% failure on commit (timeout). Retrying.

aditi_cs: Notifying affected customers: sending note that we're mitigating and may see elevated latencies for ~30m.

liam: Kickstarted emergency VM quota request to cloud provider (support case #CL-99823). No ETA yet.

sara: Workaround: spin up an on-demand pool in us-east as cross-region fallback. Spinning now: ```infractl create-pool --name emergency-us-east --gpu-type A10G --count 12 --labels=fallback=preempt-surge```. This will add capacity but routing will add latency for some customers.

ops-monitor: New pool creation accepted, provisioning started.

maya: CS confirms 2 customers saw errors clear after throttles and 60% routing to dedicated. Latency for others improved but queue still ~400.

liam: Autoscaler still gets 429s; cloud support responded: "we're throttled due to rapid provisioning requests across multiple customers, ETA 20m." Suggest we slow down scale requests and rely on emergency pool.

sara: Switching autoscaler to conservative mode to reduce API pressure: ```kubectl patch deploy autoscaler-controller -p '{"spec":{"replicas":1}}' && autoscalerctl set-mode conservative```. This reduces churn.

maya: Temporary manual steps we've taken: - applied rate-limits to long-seq endpoints - updated routing policy to send majority short-seq traffic to dedicated - prevented spot batch redeploys to drained pools - spun emergency us-east pool - opened cloud quota ticket - set autoscaler conservative.

aditi_cs: Current customer impact summary: 3 enterprise tenants degraded (higher latency), 6 self-serve customers with intermittent 500s. Estimated affected percentage of hosted traffic ~8-12% at peak.

liam: Is there any further mitigation needed now or should we hand off to follow-up oncall?

maya: Hold for 10m while emergency pool finishes. If provisioning completes, we'll shift more traffic to us-east and drain queues.

ops-monitor: emergency-us-east pool ready. Instance provisioning time ~9m.

sara: Routing updated: additional 40% of queued traffic being sent to us-east emergency pool for seq<=1024. Expect queue drain in ~6-8m.

aditi_cs: CS updated customers: we routed some traffic to a different region to reduce errors; told them to expect a normalizing window of ~15m.

maya: Queue now 72. Token latency back to baseline for short seq, long-seq still slower but improving.

liam: Ok good. I'll document runbook failure mode: autoscaler 429s during provider-wide provisioning causes inability to backfill preempted spot instances. Action items: 1) add exponential backoff + jitter to scale requests 2) emergency cross-region pool automation 3) alert for spot-churn spikes earlier 4) review quota request process.

sara: Created issue INFRA-5021 for autoscaler backoff + INFRA-5022 for emergency-pool orchestration runbook.

maya: Handing off to overnight on-call @liam for monitoring and customer comms. Please keep this thread updated with any regressions.

liam: Acknowledged. Follow-up notes: estimated impact window 00:12-00:50 UTC, root cause: cloud-side provisioning throttle + spot preemption surge + insufficient automated fallback. Postmortem required. I'll schedule a blameless postmortem and link doc in next 24h.

IncBot: Incident status set to "mitigated" by liam. Incident ID INC-2026-0315-09.

aditi_cs: Adding final customer notes and links to tickets in the incident doc.

maya: Thanks team.

liam: Leaving a quick runbook snippet for next steps: ```# if autoscaler hits 429s: 1) set autoscaler mode conservative 2) create emergency pool in another region 3) update routing policies to shift short-seq first 4) throttle long-seq endpoints 5) open cloud support case and request quota bump with "expedite" tag```

aditi_cs: Closing the customer-facing incident email draft, will send once postmortem has root-cause. :white_check_mark:
